title: Relative vanishing for the integral twist of a projective graph
statement: Let S be Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], g:S -> T separated, p:Y -> S proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], N finite, and j:Y -> P(N;T) a closed embedding satisfying j followed by projection = p followed by g [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. For L=j^*rho^*O(1) [def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-pc-module-pullback] and injective resolutions of Y.Modules, there is n0 such that every n >= n0 and q>0 has R^q p_*(L tensor-power n)=0.

source.place: Tags 02O5, graph construction of L, and 02O1, Lemma 30.16.2

proof.text: Use the existing proved private helpers AlgebraicGeometry.tensorPullback_invertible and AlgebraicGeometry.homOfGlobalSection_appTop_one from ProjectiveAmpleInvertible, imported with import all; do not restate either helper. For any finite coordinate type, use the standard coordinate sections of the integral projective twist. Pulling their nonvanishing loci through the tensor-pullback adjunction identifies them with the inverse images of the standard affine charts. These charts cover the source, are affine over an affine base, and form a finite family. Their pulled-back sections, transported through the right unitor, witness ampleness with exponent one. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies tensor pullback with ordinary pullback. This argument also treats the empty coordinate type, where the cover forces the source empty.

Separatedness of g gives the closed graph lift over S. Restrict it to an affine open V and base change it to projective space over V. Apply the preceding chart argument there. The integral-model projection identities, pullback composition and restriction/pullback comparison identify this ample module with L restricted to p inverse-image V; transport ampleness across the resulting isomorphism.

Properness over Noetherian S makes Y locally Noetherian. The tensor unit is invertible, quasi-coherent and finitely presented, hence coherent by the locally Noetherian coherence criterion. For each affine V of S apply the independent affine-open twist-vanishing theorem to that unit and L, obtaining a local threshold d(V).

Compactness of S selects finitely many affine opens covering S. Set n0 to the Finset supremum of their thresholds, zero for an empty selection. Every selected restriction vanishes for n >= n0 and q > 0. The proved library theorem Modules.isZero_of_iSup_eq_top glues their vanishing. Map the left unitor of L.tensorPow n through higherDirectImage to remove the unit tensor factor.

proof_origin.place: Tag 02O5 graph-twist construction and Tag 02O1 finite-affine-cover proof
proof_origin.note: Q3 made the coordinate-chart and finite-cover steps into Lean, generalized the existing ProjectiveAmpleInvertible coordinate proof to any finite coordinate type locally, and split only one affine-open vanishing step. No use of general proper coherence or the stronger ChowRelativeAmple theorem. Repair: removed both duplicate private helpers and used the originals through import all ProjectiveAmpleInvertible; the arbitrary-finite-coordinate chart argument remains local.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_isZero_higherDirectImage_graph_twist
    {Y S T : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian S]
    (g : S ⟶ T) [IsSeparated g] (p : Y ⟶ S) [IsProper p]
    (N : Type u) [Finite N] (j : Y ⟶ ℙ(N; T)) [IsClosedImmersion j]
    (hj : j ≫ (ℙ(N; T) ↘ T) = p ≫ g)
    [HasInjectiveResolutions Y.Modules] :
    let L := (pullback j).obj
      ((pullback (ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt N T)).obj
        (Proj.twist (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule N (ULift.{u} ℤ)) 1))
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n → ∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q →
      IsZero ((higherDirectImage p q).obj (L.tensorPow n))
